description: Eighth-round conservative temporal backfill candidates for remaining non-CN/non-CA research_temporal_dates gaps. This report is research-only and is not merged into temporal overrides.
scope_notes: Input records were checked against data/reports/military_base_temporal_priority_queue.csv and data/reports/military_base_temporal_priority_queue.json.
Rows classified as manual, nonstandard, or artifact were excluded.
Included source_ids were checked against webapp/static_public/data/map_overlays/military_base_temporal_overrides.json and were not present there at generation time.
For airport-directory and DAFIF-derived records, start_year is a conservative documented-by year rather than an inferred construction year.

candidates.name: Bonn-Hardthoehe Air Base

source_notes.title: Hardthoehe (barracks)
source_notes.note: The Hardthoehe property is identified as a German military headquarters/barracks, with barracks construction beginning in 1956 and use continuing to the present.

source_notes.title: Bundesministerium der Verteidigung - Bonn.wiki
source_notes.note: Bonn.wiki records that relocation of the Federal Ministry of Defence from Ermekeilkaserne to Hardthoehe began in 1960.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is named as an air-base/heliport feature, but the strongest temporal evidence is for the underlying Hardthoehe defence property rather than flight operations. The 1956 start is therefore a conservative facility start for the military site, with no sourced closure.

candidates.name: Jungwon Air Base

source_notes.title: Jungwon Air Base
source_notes.note: The air-base entry identifies Jungwon/Choongwon/K-75 as a Republic of Korea Air Force base and cites DAFIF airport data current as of October 2006.

source_notes.title: New RoKAF Reconnaissance Wing - Scramble
source_notes.note: Scramble reported in 2020 that Chungju/Jungwon (K-75) was already home base for RoKAF fighter/reconnaissance assets.

candidates.rationale: No reliable public establishment date was found in this pass. The candidate uses 2006 as a documented-by operational date from DAFIF-linked airport data and leaves the endpoint open.

candidates.name: Helwan

source_notes.title: Helwan Airfield
source_notes.note: The airfield entry identifies Helwan as a former RAF Helwan/Egyptian Air Force airfield, built and used from 1919 to present.

source_notes.title: Helwan Airfield | Military Wiki
source_notes.note: The mirrored military-history entry repeats the RAF Helwan identity and World War II operational context.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is Helwan, Egypt, classified as a likely air base or airfield. The 1919 date is direct built/used evidence for the named military airfield; no sourced closure was found.

candidates.name: Sidi Barrani

source_notes.title: Battle of Sidi Barrani
source_notes.note: The battle history records an airfield at Sollum/Sidi Barrani area in the 1940 Western Desert campaign context.

source_notes.title: Luftwaffe Airfields 1935-45 - Libya and Egypt
source_notes.note: The Luftwaffe airfield compilation indexes Sidi Barrani-area wartime airfields, supporting a documented World War II airfield phase.

candidates.rationale: Included conservatively because the queue row is a clean likely airfield and multiple WWII references support a Sidi Barrani-area airfield by 1940. Confidence is low because the public evidence is area-level and wartime rather than a precise modern-base establishment record.

candidates.name: Kucova

source_notes.title: 65th Anniversary of Kucova Air Base establishment - Albanian Ministry of Defence
source_notes.note: Albania's Ministry of Defence says the Aviation Regiment '23 Peza', now Kucova Air Base, was established on 15 May 1955.

source_notes.title: Albania turns an old Soviet-era air base into a regional hub of NATO air operations - AP
source_notes.note: AP reported the refurbished Kucova base was inaugurated in 2024 and quotes the Albanian prime minister saying it had been officially closed in 2005.

candidates.rationale: The queue row is Kucova, a clean likely air-base row. The Albanian MOD supplies the establishment date and AP supplies the closure/reactivation context, so intervals are included while the top-level end_year remains open due to 2024 reactivation.

candidates.name: RAF Gibraltar

source_notes.title: Airport History - Gibraltar Air Terminal
source_notes.note: The airport history says the airfield was originally opened in 1939 as an emergency airfield for the Royal Navy's Fleet Air Arm.

source_notes.title: RAF Gibraltar - Royal Air Force
source_notes.note: The RAF station page identifies RAF Gibraltar as an active RAF station.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names RAF Gibraltar. The airport history gives a clear 1939 opening date and the RAF page supports continuing station status.

candidates.name: Dübendorf Air Base

source_notes.title: Duebendorf Air Base
source_notes.note: The air-base entry says Duebendorf has been used as an air base by the Swiss Air Force since 1914 and that fighter-aircraft history there ended in 2005.

source_notes.title: History of the Swiss Air Force 1914-2022
source_notes.note: The Swiss Air Force history document begins its chronology in 1914 and references Swiss Confederation acquisition of the Duebendorf area.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Duebendorf Air Base. The start year is supported as Swiss military aviation use; no full base closure date is used because later sources indicate changed roles rather than complete closure.

candidates.name: Comandante Espora Naval Air Base

source_notes.title: 82 anos de la Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora - Argentina.gob.ar
source_notes.note: The Argentine government anniversary article describes the late-1938/early-1939 development of the site and the conversion of the base into the region's aeronaval operations center.

source_notes.title: Base Aeronaval Comandante Espora
source_notes.note: The base entry gives a creation date of 16 June 1939 and identifies the site as an Argentine Naval Aviation base.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Comandante Espora Naval Air Base. The Argentine government anniversary article and secondary base entry agree on a 1939 origin, with no sourced closure.

candidates.name: Punta Indio Naval Air Base

source_notes.title: Creacion de la Base Aeronaval Punta Indio - Phantom
source_notes.note: The article says formal creation of Base Aeronaval Punta Indio occurred on 25 February 1925 with the transfer of the Naval Aerostation School to Punta Indio.

source_notes.title: Punta Indio Naval Air Base
source_notes.note: The base entry identifies Punta Indio as a military airport operated by Argentine Naval Aviation and describes it as established in the 1920s.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Punta Indio Naval Air Base. The 1925 start is used as a conservative formal-creation date, with medium confidence because the strongest exact-date source is a specialist news/history site rather than a current official base page.

candidates.name: Base Aérea do Galeão

source_notes.title: Efemerides - INCAER
source_notes.note: INCAER's chronology records that Decree-Law 4.915 of 5 November 1942 created air-base corps for immediate installation, including the 12th C.B. Ae. at Rio de Janeiro (Galeao).

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Base Aerea do Galeao. The source establishes the Galeao air-base corps in 1942; no closure is used because the row represents the continuing Galeao air-base site.

candidates.name: Galeão Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Efemerides - INCAER
source_notes.note: INCAER's chronology records the 5 November 1942 creation of the 12th C.B. Ae. at Rio de Janeiro (Galeao).

candidates.rationale: This is a second queue source_id for the Galeao air-base site. It is included separately because the report matches on source_id and both source_ids were absent from current overrides.

candidates.name: Manaus Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Regimento Interno da Base Aerea de Manaus - SISLAER/CENDOC
source_notes.note: The FAB internal regulation says Base Aerea de Manaus was created by Decree-Law 6.814 of 21 August 1944.

source_notes.title: Base Aerea de Manaus celebra 55 anos - FAB
source_notes.note: A 2025 FAB article says the modern Manaus base marked 55 years in 2025 and notes that FAB participation in Amazonia began earlier.

candidates.rationale: The legal creation date is 1944, while the modern base anniversary source indicates later modernization/implantation context. The candidate uses the legal creation year and leaves the endpoint open.

candidates.name: Natal Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Efemerides - INCAER
source_notes.note: INCAER records the 1942 creation of air-base corps for immediate installation, including the 9th C.B. Ae. at Natal.

source_notes.title: Base Aerea de Natal - Historia da Forca Aerea Brasileira
source_notes.note: The BANT history states that the Natal base nucleus was created by Decree-Law 4.142 of 2 March 1942 and officially transformed into Base Aerea de Natal on 5 November 1942.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Natal Air Force Base. The 1942 start is well supported by FAB chronology/history material, and no sourced closure was found.

candidates.name: Porto Velho Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Decreto No. 89.684, de 17 de Maio de 1984
source_notes.note: The decree states that Base Aerea de Porto Velho (BAPV) is created with headquarters in Porto Velho, Rondonia.

source_notes.title: Base Aerea de Porto Velho - Historia da Forca Aerea Brasileira
source_notes.note: The base history gives the same 17 May 1984 creation date and says the base was inaugurated on 31 October 1984.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Porto Velho Air Force Base. A legal decree and a base-history page provide aligned 1984 creation/inauguration evidence.

candidates.name: Santa Cruz Air Force Base

source_notes.title: Conheca a estrutura, o funcionamento e as acoes sociais da Base Aerea de Santa Cruz - FAB
source_notes.note: FAB says Santa Cruz became seat of the 1st Aviation Regiment after creation of the Ministry of Aeronautics and later received the 1st Fighter Aviation Group.

source_notes.title: Projeto de Resolucao No. 05/2007 - ALERJ
source_notes.note: ALERJ states that Base Aerea de Santa Cruz was created by federal Decree-Law 5.198 of 16 January 1943, while recognizing earlier military use in 1942.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Santa Cruz Air Force Base. The formal 1943 decree date is used instead of earlier site-use references to stay conservative.

candidates.name: Santa Maria Air Force Base

operational_intervals.label: Base Aerea de Santa Maria phase
ALA 4 / continuing FAB air-base successor phase

source_notes.title: Base Aerea de Santa Maria: Santa Maria, RS - IBGE Biblioteca
source_notes.note: IBGE records that Base Aerea de Santa Maria was created on 18 December 1970 by Presidential Decree 67.877, activated on 14 July 1971, and inaugurated on 15 October 1971.

source_notes.title: Base Aerea de Santa Maria
source_notes.note: The base entry says the base was deactivated in 2016 and became ALA 4, while the airfield/base function continued under the new designation.

candidates.rationale: The queue row exactly names Santa Maria Air Force Base. The legal creation date and successor designation are both documented, so intervals distinguish the named-base phase from the continuing successor phase.
